title: Why Are We So Groupish?
frozenBasis: Official table of contents confirms chapter title and placement.
Official introduction supports the claim that morality binds groups as well as guiding individuals.
Official Chapter 9 preview supports the move toward multilevel selection and the tension between selfishness and groupishness.
supportablePoints: Chapter 9 reopens morality through the problem of human groupishness.
The chapter likely argues that humans are pulled between self-interest and group-binding tendencies.
The chapter introduces multilevel selection as a framework for understanding this tension.
The chapter shifts from partisan moral foundations into the social and evolutionary logic of group life.
unsupportedZones: No overclaiming scientific certainty for any single evolutionary account beyond the chapter-local frame.
No importing later hive-switch or religion claims as if Chapter 9 fully proves them already.
No flattening the chapter into a slogan about tribalism without the selfishness-versus-groupishness tension.
